fictional_reviews.text: The prettiest match-3 I have opened in a browser tab. Moonlit Garden bled into Crystal Echoes before I noticed an hour had passed, and firing a charged Supernova never gets old.
Gorgeous and relaxing, but it is one swap-and-match loop across twelve levels. Once you have seen the prism, the frost is just a slower version of the same evening.
A tiny universe done right: cascades that sing, goals that stay fair, and a garden I want as my desktop. The cozy match-3 all other tabs should fear.

how_to_play: Open https://lumina-cosmic-garden.vercel.app/ in a browser with JavaScript enabled; no install or account is needed.
Swap two neighbouring crystals by tapping them one after the other or by swiping (keyboard: move with arrow keys, press Enter to select, then an arrow key to swap).
Match 3 or more crystals of the same type to collect light; cascades chain automatically and charge the Supernova meter.
Match 4 in a row for a ray of light, a T or L shape for a cosmic blast, and 5 in a row for a rainbow prism.
Complete all level goals (collect light score, gather pink crystals, clear frost) before moves run out; charge Supernova to 100% and trigger it for a full-board burst.
Use Hint to reveal a match, Restart for a fresh board, the level grid to replay any of the 12 levels, and Settings for sound, motion and graphics options.
mechanics: 8x8 swap-and-match core on six crystal types with tap-to-select, swipe, and arrow-key plus Enter keyboard input
12-level Constellation I progression with per-level move limits, score targets, crystal quotas and frost counts
Three goal types: collect light (score), gather a target crystal color, and clear frost tiles
Special pieces: 4-in-a-row ray (row/column clearer), T/L-shape bomb blast, 5-in-a-row rainbow prism with prism-merge clears
Supernova meter charged by matches and cascades, firing a full-board burst at 100%
Cascade resolution with falling refills, combo callouts, floating score text and automatic reshuffle when no legal move exists
Hint finder, restart, pause, level-select grid, personal-best persistence and sound/settings controls

rating.reason: A complete, polished single-loop match-3: 12 levels with three goal types, three special pieces, Supernova meter, cascades, hint/restart/level-select and persisted bests, rendered with a cohesive cosmic presentation. Excluding the target, it sits clearly above narrow single-board casuals such as 2048 (38), Taipo (35) and T-Rex Runner (35) on progression and systems, alongside complete single-loop games such as Kart Royale (50), Deep Dive (50) and PirateSeas (50), just below Emberwake (53) and DRIFTWING (52), and well below broader-scope games such as Forja Abisal (56), LUMENRIFT (58) and catalog-top moorestech (64). Nowhere near AAA: no narrative, multiplayer, or deep meta systems. Evidence gaps: no public source repository (GitHub repository search returns zero matches and gh CLI has no auth in this environment), so engine/version claims rest on page evidence only; one headless render confirms the board runs but proves nothing about performance, balance, audio quality or long-session stability.

reconstructed_prompt: Build a cozy single-page web match-3 called LUMINA Bloom of the Cosmos: 8x8 board of six crystal types with tap, swipe and arrow-key plus Enter swapping; 12 levels with move limits and score, crystal-color and frost-clear goals; 4-match rays, T/L bombs and 5-match rainbow prisms; cascade scoring with a Supernova meter that fires a full-board burst; hint, restart, pause, level select, personal bests and sound settings; dreamy moonlit-garden cosmic art with gold serif UI and WebGL gem rendering.

screenshot_based_score.reason: Scored from a headless-Chromium render of the live playable page (1280x900, full 8x8 board of glossy distinct gems on a dark gold-trimmed tray with goals, moves, Supernova bar and cosmic backdrop all legible) plus the inspected 1672x941 cosmos.png scenery layer (moon, nebula, floating waterfall islands, glowing crystals, reflective water). Coherent stylized art direction and composed full-page scene lift it far above flat UIs such as 2048 (45), chess rot (40) and Blackjack/Beachy (35), and above Taipo (55); it matches the cohesive-stylized tier of LUMENRIFT, Sakura Rally and OUT OF THE BOX (68) but trails true 3D-scene leaders moorestech (76) and DRIFTWING (72). Still images only; motion, animation feel and audio cannot be judged.

screenshots.observation: Inspected 1672x941 PNG, the game's own fixed full-page scenery backdrop: giant glowing full moon, purple-blue nebula and starfield, floating rock islands with waterfalls, luminescent flowers and purple/cyan crystals around reflective water. This is the ambient art layer visible behind the match board during play, not the board itself; the 8x8 gem board, HUD and side panels were separately verified in a live headless render of the page.

source_analysis.finding: Page title is LUMINA Bloom of the Cosmos, described as an original game of crystals, cascades and constellations: make matches, unleash Supernova and explore the cosmic garden.

Playable match-3 loop is documented in-page: goals 01/12, collect light 0/2600, pink crystals 0/14, clear the frost 0/8, personal best, 24 moves, Match 3 crystals hint, 4-crystal ray, T/L-shape blast, 5-crystal prism, Supernova charge meter, Hint and Restart buttons.

Board is an 8 by 8 application widget: tap two neighbouring crystals or swipe; keyboard uses arrow keys, Enter to select, then an arrow key to swap; CSS uses touch-action none on board and canvas with responsive mobile breakpoints.

Embedded game data defines 12 levels (Moonlit Garden through Bloom of the Cosmos) with per-level moves, score targets, crystal quotas and frost counts, plus match-resolution, special-piece (row/col/bomb/prism), cascade, reshuffle and save-restore logic.
Page bundles a Three.js-licensed module script with extensive THREE/WebGL usage rendering the board canvas, plus AudioContext-driven sound behind a mute toggle and localStorage persistence.
Scenery backdrop is served from ./cosmos.png (1672x941 PNG, moonlit cosmic garden with floating islands, waterfalls, crystals and reflective water) and referenced as the fixed full-page background.

Headless Chromium load of the page renders the full game (LUMINA header, Moonlit Garden goals panel, LIGHT 0, 24 MOVES, complete 8x8 gem board, Supernova bar, cosmic-garden side panel), confirming the URL opens the playable game, not a promo page.

Unauthenticated GitHub repository search for lumina-cosmic-garden returns total_count 0 with no items (gh CLI has no auth token in this environment), so no verified related source repository is established.
No multiplayer, accounts, motion-sensor, or gamepad features appear anywhere in the inspected page; scoring is solo Light score plus personal best, establishing single-player with one human player.
